plan.title: fix(harness,onboarding): gate mutation readiness on functional agent hooks and Codex trust review

narratives.Description: fix(harness,onboarding): gate mutation readiness on functional agent hooks and Codex trust review
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Directive deposits agent-host hooks during `directive init` / `deft update`, and `doctor --full` now complements structural inspection with a live `deft-hook` allow/deny probe (#2852).

Mutation onboarding still does not treat **enabled** hook readiness as a deterministic prerequisite:

1. `session:start` performs no agent-hook verification.
2. `verify:session-ritual --tier=gated` invokes bare `doctor`, not `doctor --full`.
3. Bare doctor may be throttle-skipped.
4. Missing, drifted, or non-functional hooks are doctor **warnings**, so doctor exits 0 when no unrelated errors exist.
5. Codex project-hook trust remains manual and cannot be inferred from `.codex/hooks.json`.

Consequently, the gated ritual / `session:ready` can report mutation-ready while the Tier-1 enforcement surface it assumes is missing, non-functional, or untrusted.

### What already exists (do not reinvent)

- `deft verify:hooks-installed --scope=agent` already **fail-closes on structural** registration problems (`evaluateAgentHooks`).
- `doctor --full` already has the **live probe** (#2852) via `probeAgentHooksLive` (Cursor codec today).
- `plan.policy.hostHooks` per-host opt-out already exists (#2752); defaults all **enabled**.
- Default CLI/task scope for `verify:hooks-installed` remains **`git`** — agent wiring must pass `--scope=agent` or `--scope=all` explicitly.

The real gap is not "no hooks check exists." It is: (1) structural verify is not on the mutation-ready path; (2) live functionality is advisory and gated behind `doctor --full`; (3) Codex trust is documented but not modeled as a distinct readiness state.

## Parent / residual framing

- Residual hardening outside closed Core T1 epic **#2437** (not a reopen of that epic).
- Complements ceremony recovery **#2993** (`session:ready`) — readiness must not claim green when Tier-1 hooks are not actually functional.
- Adjacent only to **#2769** (post-compact reinjection); keep separate.

## Reproduction

### Missing registration

1. Initialize a consumer project.
2. Remove `.codex/hooks.json` while `plan.policy.hostHooks.codex` remains enabled.
3. Run `deft session:start`.
4. Run `deft verify:session-ritual -- --tier=gated`.

The doctor step records success because hook registration drift is advisory. (Note: `verify:hooks-installed --scope=agent` would already fail here — it is simply not wired into the ritual.)

### Non-functional hook binary

1. Leave all deposited hook files structurally current.
2. Make the installed `deft-hook` produce empty or invalid output.
3. Run the normal gated ritual without forcing `doctor --full`.

The live probe does not run, so the doctor step can record success.

### Doctor throttle

1. Run doctor once to populate doctor state.
2. Introduce hook drift.
3. Run the gated ritual inside the doctor throttle window.

Bare doctor is throttle-skipped and does not inspect agent hooks.

## Desired outcome

Enabled agent-host hooks have a dedicated, deterministic readiness gate. Doctor remains a diagnostic surface; onboarding/session readiness does not depend on doctor warning severity or throttle state.

## Scope (accept with this split)

### In scope (primary story)

1. Fail-closed **functional** agent-hook readiness (structural + live), reusing #2852.
2. Wire into mutation readiness: post-deposit init/update report, `session:ready`, gated ritual step (not cold `session:start`).
3. Honest **reporting** of Codex trust as a distinct state (registration ≠ functional ≠ trusted ≠ interception coverage).
4. Honor existing `hostHooks` opt-out (#2752) — see Opt-out contract below.
5. Docs + tests for the above.

### Out of scope / follow-up (do not block primary ship)

- A full `hooks:trust-ack` product surface as a **default hard gate** for mutation-ready.
- Machine-inferred Codex trust (not possible today).
- Reopening ceremony wall-clock work from #2990/#2991; live probes must not undo those wins.

Trust-ack (hash-bound operator attestation) may be filed as a **child/follow-up** with explicit policy if product still wants it. It must not be required for every consumer just because Codex is default-enabled in `hostHooks`.

## Proposed implementation

### 1. First-class readiness command

**Extend** the existing verifier (do not invent a second structural path):

`deft verify:hooks-installed --scope=agent --live`

It should:

- structurally inspect every **enabled** host deposit (existing `evaluateAgentHooks`);
- on structural green, run the live probe by invoking the installed `deft-hook` shim, not its resolved source file;
- reuse `probeAgentHooksLive` / #2852 rather than forking a second subprocess/codec path;
- exercise allow and deny fixtures;
- validate host-specific decision codecs for at least Cursor and Codex (expand beyond Cursor-only);
- return non-zero for missing, drifted, unavailable, or non-functional **enabled** hooks;
- treat `plan.policy.hostHooks.<host> = false` as intentional disabled, not a failure;
- apply the same **consumer vs maintainer** rule as doctor: maintainer framework source checkouts skip consumer deposit fail-closed (consumer-only surface).

### 2. Wire mutation onboarding

Run the readiness gate:

- after `directive init` / `deft update` deposits hooks (report post-deposit result);
- from `deft session:ready`;
- as a gated ritual prerequisite (record green only when readiness passes).

Do **not** put the live probe on cold `session:start` (ceremony cost; #2990).

Do **not** route this through bare doctor: doctor throttling and advisory severity are appropriate for diagnostics, not for a fail-closed gate.

### 3. Ceremony / latency constraints

Throttle-independent is required for **correctness**, but every `session:ready` / gated path must not reintroduce multi-second process tax:

- Structural fail-fast first; live probe only after structural green.
- Optional short TTL cache of a green live-probe result **inside the current ritual-state freshness window** — must **not** inherit doctor's 4h/24h throttle.
- Document an expected probe budget; multi-host expansion must stay within it.

### 4. Represent Codex trust honestly

Codex trust cannot currently be machine-read. Expose it as a **distinct report state**:

- `functional-untrusted` or `manual-review-required`;
- actionable instruction: open `/hooks` and approve the exact project hook;
- never describe Codex hooks as active solely because `.codex/hooks.json` exists and the command works.

**v1 readiness hard-fail rules:** fail closed on missing / drifted / non-functional **enabled** hooks. Trust is reported distinctly; it is **not** a default hard gate for all consumers with default-enabled Codex.

Optional follow-up: hash-bound operator acknowledgement, e.g. `deft hooks:trust-ack --host codex`. If added:

- label it operator-attested, not machine-verified;
- stale when the managed Codex hook definition hash changes;
- only apply when policy requires it and/or the active host is Codex — never block Cursor-only or Claude-only operators solely because Codex remains default-enabled;
- never apply to opted-out hosts.

### 5. Opt-out contract (#2752)

Consumers already have persistent per-host opt-out via `plan.policy.hostHooks` (hosts: `claude`, `cursor`, `grok`, `codex`; default all enabled). Inspect with `deft policy:show --field=hostHooks`. This readiness work must reuse that policy — do not invent a second opt-out flag.

Readiness rules:

- Only **enabled** hosts can fail the readiness gate.
- `hostHooks.<host> = false` is intentional disabled: report healthy/disabled, never recommend `deft update` repair for that host.
- Recovery copy when an enabled host fails and the operator does not use that host must also point at opt-out (`policy:show --field=hostHooks` / set that host to `false`), not only `deft update`.
- Any Codex trust-ack or trust hard-gate (if implemented) must **not** apply to opted-out hosts, and must **not** block mutation solely because default-enabled Codex is present but unused.
- Opt-out is independent of git hooks (`.githooks/`) and of `hostSlashCommands` slash deposit.

## Acceptance criteria

### Primary (ship-blocking)

- [ ] Removing an enabled `.codex/hooks.json` makes agent-hook readiness exit non-zero.
- [ ] Drifted Codex SessionStart or PreToolUse matchers make readiness exit non-zero.
- [ ] Empty, invalid, or wrong allow/deny output from the installed hook shim makes readiness exit non-zero.
- [ ] At least Cursor and Codex host-specific decision envelopes are live-tested (reuse #2852; no forked probe path).
- [ ] Opted-out hosts (`plan.policy.hostHooks.<host> = false`) remain explicitly healthy/disabled and never fail readiness.
- [ ] Failure recovery prose mentions opt-out via `deft policy:show --field=hostHooks` when the operator does not need that host.
- [ ] `session:ready` cannot report mutation-ready when an enabled hook is missing or non-functional.
- [ ] Gated ritual records agent-hook readiness green only when the readiness gate passes.
- [ ] The gate does not inherit doctor's 4h/24h throttle.
- [ ] Init/update report the post-deposit readiness result.
- [ ] Codex trust is **reported** separately from registration and command functionality (not conflated as "active").
- [ ] Live probe is not invoked from cold `session:start`.
- [ ] Structural check fails before live probe runs (fail-fast).
- [ ] Maintainer framework source checkouts do not fail closed for missing consumer deposits (same consumer-context rule as doctor).
- [ ] Tests cover missing, drifted, non-functional, opted-out, and throttle-independent paths.
- [ ] Documentation distinguishes: registration → command functionality → host trust → interception coverage.

### Follow-up only (not primary ship)

- [ ] Trust-ack / trust hard-gates (if any) skip opted-out hosts and do not fail readiness for unused default-enabled hosts.
- [ ] Any manual trust acknowledgement is bound to the exact managed hook hash and is labeled operator-attested.
- [ ] Tests cover trusted-ack and stale-ack when the follow-up lands.

## Related

- #2437 / #2438 — Tier-1 host-hook enforcement (closed; this issue is residual)
- #2596 — Codex lifecycle hook adapter and trust-aware structural reporting
- #2752 — persistent per-host opt-out
- #2852 — `doctor --full` live probe
- #2769 — post-compact context reinjection; adjacent but separate
- #2990 / #2991 / #2992 / #2993 — ceremony cost, re-arm, `session:ready` (do not regress wall-clock wins)

## Issue comment thread

_The issue body is the original write-up; maintainer comments below may supersede it. Read the full thread before building a dispatch envelope (#2143)._

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-03T21:13:10Z)

## Evaluation (accept with amendments — applied to body)

### Verdict
**Do not accept the original undivided scope as-is.** Accept the problem statement and primary functional-readiness story; demote default hard-gate trust-ack to follow-up. Body updated accordingly.

### Facts checked against current code
| Claim | Status |
|--------|--------|
| `session:start` has no agent-hook verification | True |
| Gated ritual runs bare `doctor` (`["doctor"]`), not `--full` | True |
| Bare doctor can be throttle-skipped | True |
| Registration + live probe are doctor **warnings** (exit 0) | True |
| Live probe only under `doctor --full`, Cursor codec only | True (#2852) |
| `session:ready` can go green without functional hooks | True |
| Structural `verify:hooks-installed --scope=agent` already fail-closes | True — gap is wiring + live, not inventing structure |
| `hostHooks` per-host opt-out exists (#2752), default all enabled | True |

### Related open work
- No open issue owns this exact readiness gate.
- #2769 adjacent only (post-compact reinjection).
- Closed #2437 residual; closed #2990–#2993 ceremony path must not regress.

### Why trust-ack was split out
Defaults enable all hosts including Codex. Requiring operator trust-ack for mutation-ready whenever `hostHooks.codex` is true would block Cursor-only / Claude-only consumers. Attestation is also not verification — reporting trust distinctly is enough for v1.

### Labels applied
`bug`, `harness`, `agent-experience`, `determinism`, `doctor`, `process`, `area:cli`, `adoption-blocker`

### Body amendments included
1. What already exists (do not reinvent)
2. Parent / residual framing (#2437 residual, #2993 complement)
3. Primary vs follow-up scope split
4. Ceremony / latency constraints (no cold session:start live probe; structural fail-fast; optional ritual-window TTL ≠ doctor throttle)
5. Trust report vs default hard-gate
6. Opt-out contract (#2752)
7. Primary vs follow-up acceptance criteria
8. Maintainer vs consumer skip rule
